prompt_text: Who is a reliable contractor in Joplin MO for a home remodel or repair project?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first: what kind of project is it (full remodel, kitchen, bathroom, roof, foundation, small repairs)? That matters for which contractors to target (general contractor vs. a tradesperson).

If you want an immediate answer: I can’t browse the web right now to pull up current contractor listings and reviews, so I don’t want to give a single name that might be out of date. Instead, here’s a reliable, practical way to find and choose a trustworthy contractor in Joplin, MO — plus the vetting checklist and questions to ask so you can pick someone confidently.

Where to look (local and reputable sources)
- Better Business Bureau (BBB) — check ratings and complaints.
- Angi / HomeAdvisor — contractor profiles, reviews, and cost ranges.
- Google Maps and Yelp — recent customer reviews and photos of completed projects.
- Houzz — good for remodel specialists and portfolios.
- Nextdoor and local Facebook community groups — local homeowner recommendations.
- Joplin Chamber of Commerce — list of member contractors.
- Missouri Home Builders Association or local builders’ associations.
- Joplin Planning & Community Development / building department — ask about required permits and get names of contractors who pull permits.
- State licensing/registration portals for specific trades (electricians, plumbers, HVAC) — verify licenses.

How to vet candidates (quick checklist)
- Ask for proof of current insurance (general liability and workers’ comp). Call the insurer to confirm.
- Verify trade licenses where required (electrician, plumber). Confirm any local registrations.
- Get at least 3 written bids so you can compare scope and price.
- Request references for similar projects (preferably from projects in Joplin or nearby). Call them and ask about timeline, workmanship, change orders, and cleanup.
- Look up BBB, Google, Yelp reviews and check for recurring complaints.
- Confirm they pull permits and pass inspections — a reliable contractor will handle that.
- Check for a local business address and how long they’ve been in business.

Red flags
- Large upfront cash-only requests (a reasonable deposit is normal, but avoid large cash demands).
- No written contract or vague scope of work.
- No proof of insurance or refusal to provide it.
- Pressuring you to sign quickly or to skip permits.
- Extremely low bids compared to others (could indicate cutting corners).

What to include in a written contract
- Detailed scope of work and materials to be used (brands and model numbers, where relevant).
- Total price, payment schedule, and acceptable payment methods.
- Project start date, major milestone dates, and estimated completion date.
- Change order process and cost approval procedure.
- Warranty on workmanship and materials.
- Agreement that contractor will obtain all necessary permits and inspections.
- Liens and release clause: final payment only after lien waivers from subs/suppliers.
- Cleanup and disposal terms.

Questions to ask a contractor
- How long have you been doing this kind of work in Joplin area?
- Can you provide 3 local references from similar projects?
- Do you carry general liability and workers’ comp? Can you provide a COI?
- Who will supervise the job daily and who is my main point of contact?
- How do you handle unexpected problems or change orders?
- Will you obtain required permits and schedule inspections?
- What is your warranty on labor and materials?

If you’d like, I can:
- Draft an RFP/email template you can send to 3–5 contractors.
- Provide a short list of questions tailored to your specific project.
- Help evaluate three bids if you paste them here.

Tell me what type of remodel/repair you need and whether you prefer a general contractor or a trade-specific pro, and I’ll help you take the next step.
